newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no trade - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no trade - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle were not trading near midday Thursday following vigorous sales Wednesday at $65.00 per cwt, feedlot sources said.
Light bids at $64.00 were passed by owners asking $65.00 to $66.00 for cattle that were left. Most feedlots were current with showlists depleted, sources said.

Sales in Kansas on Wednesday at 83,000 head set the second largest one-day volume record behind 88,000 in September 1995, USDA statistics showed. The week-to-date movement through Thursday morning was pegged near 125,000. The full week record was set June 5 this year at 146,500, USDA statistics showed.
Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma sales Wednesday were estimated at 78,700 head, with week-to-date sales of 129,200, market sources said.
Sales records in the Panhandle were not close to being toppled, sources there said.
Daily Panhandle-area record high sales were set February 22, 1996 at 104,800 head and the weekly record-large movement was set the week ended September 12, 1996 at 196,000 head, USDA data showed.
Fed cattle prices were lifted by strong packer demand to fill previously booked beef orders, sources said.
The orders reportedly were placed by retailers planning sales promotions for the Labor Day holiday weekend at the end of the month, they said.
